audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1 and 5 of the level chart credit Swain outright; the packet chart and the already-audited mirror both say Skill.
audit.why: Level 1 is a mutual poke standoff (Parrrley 625 vs Death's Hand 750, no kill threat either way) and level 6 is Swain's ultimate against a Gangplank who can simply not commit — neither is a clean win. The mirror set both rows to Skill at 5/10, so leaving them as Swain would render two different answers on the two pages.
audit.corrected: win[0]/phases[0].side and win[4]/phases[4].side to Skill, both ratings to 5/10.

audit.why: Spike order is right and honest: your level 3 W-into-E window, your level 6, then his Sheen item and his late-game barrel-plus-global phase. The page correctly gives the last two spikes to him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanical errors: Gangplank's passive is called a crit on his Q last-hit, Powder Kegs are described as if they were on a cooldown he must respect, and Swain is called a 'melee-range kit'.
audit.why: Trial by Fire is a periodic melee strike that sets the target on fire — no crit, and it is not attached to Parrrley. Powder Kegs cost 0 mana on a 0-second cooldown at 1000 range, so the limit is keg stock, not a cooldown to bait. Swain's Q is 750 and Nevermove is 850; he is not a melee-range champion, and the whole reason the lane is playable is that he matches his poke range.
audit.corrected: Passive named Trial by Fire and described as a burn; keg pressure framed as free and pre-emptive; Swain's ranges used rather than a melee framing.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere in the trade advice.
audit.why: Remove Scurvy is 22/20/18/16/14s and Nevermove is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s. That gap is the entire kill window: after he eats an Oranges your root comes back roughly twice before his cleanse does.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into whys[3] and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells the player to buy Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Remove Scurvy is a heal, and it is the reason your chip poke never converts into a kill threat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cannon Barrage is treated as ordinary map pressure.
audit.why: It deals true damage, so the MR a Swain would otherwise stack does nothing against it — relevant to how you position for objective fights, not just to lane.

edits.before: Both champions want to establish poke range from the first wave — Gangplank's barrel passive crit and Swain's W trade roughly evenly, and neither can force a kill without abilities the other can answer.
edits.after: Both want poke range from the first wave — Trial by Fire only burns on his melee strike and Parrrley reaches 625 against your 750 Q, so the chip trades evenly and neither can force a kill yet.

edits.before: His barrel chains deal pre-emptive AoE crit damage that punishes Swain's melee-range kit; Swain cannot root him cleanly while barrels control the approach path.
edits.after: Powder Kegs cost no mana and no cooldown, so he seeds your approach for free; you cannot land Nevermove's return root while kegs decide where you are allowed to stand.

edits.before: Gangplank can stack and maintain three-barrel chains faster than Swain's E cooldown, keeping Swain outside effective W-into-E range and winning the sustained poke war.
edits.after: He restacks kegs faster than Nevermove's 11-second cooldown and Remove Scurvy heals the chip back, so buy Grievous Wounds before you expect to win the sustained poke war.

edits.before: At level 1 neither of you wants a straight duel — Gangplank's passive crit on his Q last-hit and barrel chain poke match your W harass range, and without E you cannot close the gap. Respect his barrel placement: if he stacks two kegs between you and your minions, do not walk into them to last-hit; sacrifice the CS or use W from max range to detonate the kegs safely. At level 2 you get E but he still controls space with barrels — root him only when he steps forward to place a keg close to you, not when he is sitting at his natural range. Level 3 is your first real moment: W the barrel cluster to deny his setup, then E-root him in the aftermath before he re-positions. Even then, his W (Remove Scurvy) eats your root clean, so bait the first Oranges use in a small trade before committing the kill combo.
edits.after: At level 1 neither of you wants a straight duel — his Parrrley chip on a 4.5-second cooldown and his keg poke match your harass range, and without E you cannot close the gap. Respect his keg placement: if he stacks two between you and your minions, do not walk in to last-hit; sacrifice the CS or use W from max range to pop them safely. At level 2 you get E but he still owns the space — root him only when he steps forward to seed a keg close to you, never while he sits at his own range. Level 3 is your first real moment: W the keg cluster to deny the setup, then throw E past him so the return wave roots him before he re-positions. Remove Scurvy still cleanses that root, so bait the first Oranges in a small trade — it is down 22 seconds at rank 1 — before you commit the kill combo.

edits.before: Once Gangplank completes Trinity Force the lane is effectively over as a kill lane — his barrel chains with a Sheen proc will chunk you to half before your root can land, and he can Oranges every E you throw. Your role shifts to matching his wave clear and denying him free barrel stacks near your tower while farming for your own item spike. At two-plus items he becomes a global threat with his R dropping on every Dragon and Baron setup across the map; you cannot match that macro, so the correct play is to accept a farm lane from this point, group for teamfights where your AoE drain is most valuable, and let your team's composition punish his splitpush tendencies rather than trying to out-duel a fully-stacked Gangplank in the sidelane.
edits.after: Once Gangplank completes Trinity Force the lane is over as a kill lane — a keg chain with a Sheen proc chunks you to half before your root lands, and he cleanses every E you throw. Your role shifts to matching his wave clear and denying him free keg stacks near your tower while you farm your own spike. At two-plus items he is a global threat, and Cannon Barrage deals true damage on every Dragon and Baron setup, so the magic resist you might buy against him buys nothing there — stand out of the circle instead. You cannot match that macro: accept a farm lane, group for fights where your AoE drain is worth most, and let your team punish his splitpush rather than duelling a stacked Gangplank in the sidelane.

notes: Gangplank's passive was written as a crit tied to his Q last-hit; Trial by Fire is a periodic melee burn and the crit comes from kegs plus items. Powder Kegs were framed as a cooldown to bait — they are 0 mana, 0 cooldown, 1000 range, so the advice now keys off keg stock and positioning instead. Swain was called 'melee-range' in whys[2], which is wrong at Q 750 / E 850. Rows 1 and 5 of the chart flipped to Skill in matched pairs to agree with both the packet and the already-audited mirror. Left diff/diffRating alone: the mirror re-rated from Gangplank's side against a 55.26% win rate, and this side's 49.83% does not by itself justify moving 6/10.
